A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ALI relighting work despite the changed title. All 16 pages of v1 and 17 pages of v2, including equations, tables, figures and Appendices A-C, support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original relighting evaluations, backbone and training-stage ablations, material-specific analyses, qualitative results and two user studies.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental and user-study results, including the supplementary visual evaluations.

M1.justification: The feature fusion, losses, frozen/trainable components, three training stages and inference procedure are unchanged. Recasting ALI as a controlled probe does not introduce a different algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions retain MIIW and BigTime training, the IIW/RealEstate-10K/DL3DV sources for the Lighting Zoo, and the same cross-scene, in-scene and in-the-wild evaluations. Appendix examples, including the painting, are retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1-3 and Figures 3, 4 and S.2. The backbone comparison also retains Latent Intrinsics, MAE, DINOv2, DINOv3, CLIP and RADIOv2.5; v1 Table 5 becomes v2 Table 4.

E3.justification: The reported training budgets, metrics, bypass controls, 12-reference cross-scene protocol and i+12 in-scene protocol are retained. Appendix A.3 newly describes participant counts, presentation and response options for the existing studies; it does not establish that the studies were rerun or their design changed.

E4.justification: The backbone, material and training-stage ablations remain, as do lighting interpolation and supplementary qualitative cases. The backbone/material tables exchange numbers, and the dedicated multi-stage discussion is removed, but the corresponding analytical evidence remains.

E5.justification: v2 Table 3 newly marks user-study entries with significance stars defined as p < 0.05. Neither the table nor Appendix A.3 identifies the statistical test or null hypothesis. No repeated-run, seed or confidence-interval reporting is added.

E6.justification: Tables 1 and 2 and the matched backbone/material tables have identical numerical entries. Table 3 retains the same estimates with two-decimal rounding, such as 0.931 becoming 0.93. Qualitative examples are retained; the new significance-reporting practice is assessed under E5.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and Equations 1-6 are unchanged. Neither version supplies additional theorems, proofs or substantive mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that relighting probes visual representations, semantic strength can conflict with photometric fidelity, and ALI improves relighting through dense visual priors. The same MIIW performance claims remain. v2 foregrounds the probing contribution already explicitly claimed in v1.

C2.justification: v2 removes v1's explicit qualification that Stage III can reduce MIIW scores while improving in-the-wild quality. The retained material table still shows regressions, such as glossy SSIM decreasing from 0.6291 to 0.6196. v2 also makes the image-only, geometry-free applicability limitation more explicit.

D1.justification: Appendix A.3 newly discloses 23 participants, 9 and 12 pairs per participant in the respective studies, randomized full-resolution presentation and win/tie/lose responses. v2 also explicitly describes fixed controls for backbone comparisons. Training and Lighting Zoo implementation details remain unchanged, while the project-page link is removed.

R1.justification: v2 removes the DiffusionLight citation by Phongthawee et al. and its bibliography entry. Related work is recast around physical and semantic visual priors, but the remaining cited works and the claim of a first systematic generative-relighting investigation are retained.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, experimental narrative and discussion undergo extensive rewriting. Section 5 is reorganized into relighting performance and visual-prior probing, with backbone analysis moved ahead of material analysis. This substantially changes the narrative organization despite stable methods and results.

P2.justification: Table 3 changes from a wide combined table to two stacked panels with significance markers. The backbone/material tables exchange numbering and placement, Figure 2 replaces VRM labels with Visual Encoder, and Figure 3's caption is shortened. The existing visual examples remain.

improvement.justification: The participant and trial counts and presentation details added in Appendix A.3 make the paper's important perceptual evidence more assessable, while the reorganized experiments clarify the probing argument. These are limited reporting gains: significance testing remains unspecified, and removal of the Stage III regression caveat and project-page link reduces transparency in those respects.
